Priya to share RBAC least-privilege role mappings and example policies
Customer to provide test IdP metadata and SCIM attribute requirements

Priya Nair: Prepare RBAC mapping example and least-privilege roles doc - due 2027-01-04

summary: Midwest Bank and Redwood review SSO/SAML and SCIM integration surface area plus RBAC/least-privilege model. Discussed IdP options (Okta/Azure AD), SCIM attribute mapping, service account permissions, audit logging and retention, KMS key management, SOC 2 artifacts. Agreed on POC timeline and concrete next steps.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-24 15:00 EST | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam, Ellen, Carlos, Sara, Tom (Midwest Bank)
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, happy holidays  we'll run through SSO, SCIM and RBAC today, quick agenda - SSO options, SCIM provisioning, RBAC mapping, audit/logging, Q/A and next steps.
[00:22] Ellen: thanks Jordan, quick ask from my side, we need to ensure least privilege and that audit logs meet our retention policy. also, we use Okta primary and Azure AD for some teams.
[00:35] Priya: great, we'll show how Redwood supports both Okta and Azure AD. SCIM provisioning works over the SCIM 2.0 endpoint, common attributes are supported but we'll confirm the attr list.
[01:05] Carlos: one thing, we host some workloads in us-east and some in canada-west  data residency matters for a subset. do you offer region pinning?
[01:20] Jordan: yes, Redwood Private has region pinning / VPC options for data residence. For hosted, we can discuss region controls and retention settings  we'll include the specifics in the SOC 2 and data residency doc.
[02:10] Priya: on SAML, typical flow: IdP sends assertion to Redwood ACS endpoint, we validate certificate (x509). We support SAML 2.0 and can accept metadata or manual cert upload. Note: some customers call our ACs url differently in their set-up, small transcription: sometimes ACS gets transcribed as A-C-S or ACES in notes, so watch for that.
[03:00] Tom: how do you handle certificate rotation? we need automation.
[03:12] Priya: cert rotation can be automated on the IdP side; Redwood supports seamless rotation if you upload the new cert in advance and toggle. For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for keys.
[04:05] Ellen: SCIM provisioning  does it support group sync and user deprovisioning? we need immediate removal within 24 hours for terminated employees.
[04:22] Priya: yes, SCIM supports group push and user deprovisioning, you can configure deprovisioning behaviour. We'll share the SCIM attribute list  common attributes: userName, emails, name, groups, externalId, and a couple custom attrs. Our default behaviour is immediate deprovision in hosted, but on Dedicated/Private you can tune it.
[05:30] Carlos: any rate limits on SCIM calls? we have a big org so we'd prefer bulk operations.
[05:45] Priya: rate limits exist; we also support bulk/group operations for initial syncs. We'll surface suggested rate limits for Okta/Azure AD.
[06:40] Jordan: switching to RBAC  typical roles we recommend: Admin (org-level, very limited), Team Admin (manage teams and routes), DevOps/Infra (deploy/run models), Readonly/Analyst.
[07:05] Sara: can we map SAML assertions to roles via SCIM group membership? we're trying to avoid manual mapping.
[07:20] Priya: yes, best practice is SCIM groups -> Redwood roles, SCIM group names map to role names. You can also map SAML assertion attributes to roles if needed. We'll provide a mapping template.
[08:10] Tom: least-privilege is critical. For ingestion and model keys, can we restrict key usage to certain routes and IP ranges?
[08:28] Priya: yes, per-route API keys and token scoping are supported. For Dedicated/Private you can also restrict egress and set CIDR allow lists. Note: some customers refer to KV cache as KV "cash" in notes  little transcription quirk.
[09:15] Ellen: audit logs: what events are logged and what's retention? we need admin actions, user logins, token issuance, model changes, and raw request metadata for a rolling 12 months.
[09:40] Priya: Redwood audit logs cover admin actions, auth events (SSO), SCIM provisioning events, model deployments, config changes, and request-level traces. Retention: default 90 days in hosted, can extend to 12 months as add-on or in Dedicated/Private. We'll include retention tiers and pricing.
[11:05] Carlos: encryption at rest  do you manage keys or can we use our own KMS? also, in transit encryption?
[11:22] Jordan: we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS and other KMS/HSMs for Private. All traffic is TLS 1.2+; for Private you can bring your own KMS. We'll attach KMS integration docs.
[12:30] Sara: for SOC 2, can we get the Type II and the auditor contact?
[12:40] Jordan: yes, we'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and summary. Also GH: we keep an iso27001 summary as well if useful.
[13:30] Priya: quick demo note  when routing roles, you can configure policy: latency-first, cost-first, region-first. For security-sensitive customers region-first + dedicated pools is common.
[14:10] Tom: we have a requirement for SAML session length and forced re-auth every 8 hours, can we enforce?
[14:25] Priya: SAML session is honored; you can enforce session limits via IdP and set token TTLs on Redwood tokens. We'll provide recommended values.
[15:00] Ellen: compliance question  do you provide audit log export to our SIEM? we use Splunk.
[15:12] Priya: yes, logs can be pushed to your syslog/S3 or Splunk via forwarder; Dedicated has a native connector. Hosted exports via secure S3 or streaming.
[16:05] Carlos: any penetration test results or vuln remediations we can see?
[16:18] Jordan: we have pentest summaries and remediation timelines; we'll include an executive summary and contact for deeper security pack.
[17:00] Tom: SCIM attribute specifics  show me an example for groups->roles mapping.
[17:12] Priya: example: scim group name "midwest-admins" maps to Redwood role "OrgAdmin". SCIM payload snippet: groups.value = "midwest-admins" etc. We'll share config snippet for Okta/Azure.
[18:05] Ellen: provisioning automation  if someone is removed from AD, how fast is revoke? we said 24h but prefer immediate.
[18:20] Priya: immediate in most setups; there are small windows if using caching/edge caches, but we can set TTLs low. For high security, Dedicated with short cache TTLs is recommended.
[19:55] Carlos: what about developer access to logs or model prompts? we need redact PII and also enforce least-privilege so devs don't see full request payloads.
[20:10] Priya: Redwood supports field-level redaction and role-based access to logs. You can mask prompt content and store raw request only for specific roles. We'll provide the masking config.
[21:45] Jordan: costs  extra for extended audit retention, private KMS integration, and dedicated pools. We'll give pricing ranges in the follow-up.
[22:30] Tom: any gotchas with Okta group push? we've seen group names truncated sometimes.
[22:45] Priya: Okta has length limits; we'll recommend canonical names and avoid special chars. We'll include that in the quickstart.
[24:10] Ellen: can we do a short POC: wire SAML/SCIM to a test tenant, validate RBAC mapping and audit logs?
[24:25] Jordan: yes, proposed POC: week of 2027-01-04, 2-week trial, Redwood sets up test env, customer provides IdP test account.
[25:00] Carlos: timeline is tight, can you expedite docs?
[25:10] Jordan: we'll send the quickstart and SOC 2 within 48 hours. Priya will send RBAC mapping.
[26:00] (brief silence, crosstalk)
[27:00] Priya: some implementation notes: SCIM requires a service account with 'Provisioning' scope; avoid using admin user creds. For SAML, include NameID format and email attribute mapping.
[28:30] Tom: question on logging anonymization for GDPR? we need user identifiers pseudonymized for EU users.
[28:45] Priya: yes, we can pseudonymize identifiers and redact content for EU residency. We'll discuss retention and export controls.
[30:10] Ellen: do you support SCIM incremental syncs? we have a large user base.
[30:25] Priya: yes incremental syncs supported; initial full sync recommended then incremental deltas.
[32:00] Jordan: let's capture the security acceptance criteria  1) SCIM auto-provision + deprovision within 24h (prefer immediate), 2) SSO via Okta/Azure with cert rotation, 3) audit logs exported to Splunk and retained 12 months, 4) CMK support for encryption at rest, 5) RBAC least privilege mappings.
[33:15] Sara: that looks good, I'll take the acceptance criteria back to legal.
[34:00] Priya: little gotcha: for some OnPrem setups there is double NAT and SAML callback issues, we can provide network checklist.
[35:30] Tom: any SLA around access/SSO failures?
[35:45] Jordan: SLA on Dedicated, hosted has uptime commitments; we'll include SSO failover patterns  can fallback to secondary IdP.
[36:50] Carlos: do you log raw prompts for ML evals? if so we need redaction and retention rules.
[37:05] Priya: logs can include prompts for evals but can be opt-out or redacted by default. We keep eval stores isolated and require role to view.
[38:20] Ellen: who on your side will be our contact for security questionnaires?
[38:30] Jordan: me for commercial and Priya for technical. We'll loop in our security lead for deep Qs.
[39:40] (short technical back-and-forth about SCIM endpoints and example JSON)
[42:10] Priya: I'll attach sample Okta rule and Azure app manifest snippets. Also note scim base path sometimes needs trailing slash depending on IdP.
[43:55] Tom: are there logs for failed provisioning attempts? we need alerting on failures.
[44:10] Priya: yes, provisioning failures generate audit events and can trigger webhooks/alerts.
[45:20] Jordan: recap of next steps  we'll send docs, schedule POC, and start the test integration.
[46:00] Ellen: thanks, expecting the docs; can we get a kickoff invite for the POC?
[46:12] Jordan: yes, we'll send calendar invite for Jan 4th and include the POC plan.
[47:00] Tom: one more item  RBAC review for external contractors, can contractors be scoped to very limited projects?
[47:18] Priya: yes, create a contractor role with scoped resource access and time-bound tokens. We recommend short TTLs.
[48:05] Carlos: final ask  do you provide a security checklist for our infra team?
[48:18] Priya: yes, network checklist, IdP checklist, SCIM checklist, RBAC guides  we'll bundle.
[49:00] (wrap up, small pleasantries)
[49:30] Jordan: thanks everyone, happy holidays, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
[50:00] Meeting ends. Transcription notes: some words are misrecognized (KV cache -> KV cash, ACS -> ACs), speaker labels sometimes generic.
